answer: Every identity posts a 50-credit bond tied to one egress harbor in a harbor registry. An auditor replays origin logs per epoch: an umber flag marks traffic from a harbor claimed by another identity, and a shared harbor burns both bonds. Scarcity makes leases climb a spiral schedule: the first costs 25 credits, the kth 25+5(k-1), the thousandth 5,020. One honest identity pays one 25 lease and recovers its bond; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 harbors, paying 2,522,500 in leases plus 50,000 locked. A device farm routing many identities via one harbor fails: one umber collision burns the whole cluster.
